cim_eredeti: 8 Best AI Video Face Swap Tools in 2026, Prices Checked
szoveg_eredeti:
The best AI video face swap tool in 2026 depends on what you need to replace and how long the clip is. For swapping a whole character (face, hair, outfit and body) into a short clip while keeping the motion, camera and sound, Krea Video Swap and Higgsfield Genjutsu are the strongest, with Krea taking up to 4 references and Higgsfield up to 30. For a quick free face-only swap, Magic Hour gives 3 free swaps a day with no account. For long videos, Akool and Vidnoz handle minutes of footage, and VisionStory goes to 3 minutes at 1080p. Viggle is the pick for meme and dance templates.

This guide compares eight AI face swap tools for video on what actually decides the choice: free tier, longest clip, output resolution, watermark, whether it swaps only the face or the full character, and price. Every number comes from the vendor’s own pages, checked on 17 November 2026, and we link the source. Where a vendor does not publish a number, we say so instead of guessing. Krea is our product. We say where it wins and where it doesn’t, including that it has no free tier for video swaps.

Upload a video and up to 4 reference images. Krea Video Swap replaces people, outfits and objects while the motion, camera and sound stay.

We started from the tools people actually search for and compare: the pages that rank for “video face swap” and “face swap video,” and the names that come up most in “best face swap app” threads. Then we checked each one on its own site on 17 November 2026: Magic Hour’s video face swap page and pricing, Higgsfield’s Face Swap, Recast and Genjutsu announcement, VisionStory’s face swap page and pricing, Viggle’s face swap page and pricing, Akool’s face swap page and pricing, Vidnoz’s face swap page and pricing, OpenArt’s video face swap page and pricing, and Krea’s pricing.

We left out tools that market themselves around adult content or real-time impersonation, and tools that only work on photos. We did not run paid quality tests on every tool for this post, so it makes no ranking of output quality. Face swap quality changes with each model update, and the fair test is your own clip on two or three of these.

Six things decide whether a tool fits the job:

Krea Video Swap replaces people, faces, outfits, objects or the background in an existing video and keeps everything else: the original motion, camera moves, cuts and audio. You upload one source video and 1 to 4 reference images, and optionally say what goes where (“the second image replaces the man on the left”). If you don’t, Krea works out what each reference replaces. A person reference can even replace a non-person, like a car or an animal.

It runs on three models, chosen per job:

Video Swap accepts mp4, mov, webm and ogg video, and jpg, png, webp, avif and heic references. It’s also available outside the web app: through the Krea API, as the swap_video tool on Krea’s MCP server for Claude and other agents, and inside Krea Agent. To make a reference character first, generate one with Krea 3 or edit a photo with Krea’s face swap for images, then swap it into your video and upscale the result with the video upscaler.

Pricing, from krea.ai/pricing on 17 November 2026: Video Swap needs a paid plan. Basic is $9/month ($5/month billed yearly) with 5,000 compute units, Pro is $35/month ($21 billed yearly) with 20,000, and Max is $70/month ($42 billed yearly) with 40,000. A 10-second swap at 720p uses roughly 2,850 to 4,000 units depending on the model, and the panel shows the exact cost before you run it. Paid plans include a commercial license.

Where Krea stops: there is no free video swap, so you can’t test it without a plan. Clips top out at about 30 seconds, so long videos need cutting into segments or a long-form face-swap tool. There is no template library of trending clips; you bring your own footage. Close-ups and scenes with several people talking are harder cases, so expect to run a second take.

Magic Hour is the easiest way to try a video face swap for free. Its page says you get “3 free video or GIF face swaps per day in total,” “up to 10 seconds each” at 480p, and you can start with “No account required.” Free output is watermarked. A Multi mode maps each face in the video to a different source photo, and Magic Hour has separate head swap, body swap and character replace tools.

Pricing: Creator is $19/month ($12/month billed yearly), Pro $39 ($25 billed yearly), and Business $99 ($66 billed yearly), plus one-time credit packs from $10. Paid output is watermark-free, at 720p and 1080p from Creator, with 4K on Pro and above when the source supports it. There is also a face swap API from $0.023 per second. Commercial use is for paid subscribers and credit-pack buyers only.

Where it stops: the free tier is short, low-resolution and watermarked. The main face swap tool replaces only the face; full-character swaps live in a separate tool. Magic Hour states you “must have rights to the source media and every face you use.”

Higgsfield offers three tools for swapping in video. Face Swap works on photos and videos; the free tier is “5 free image face swaps per day,” and video swaps need a paid plan. Recast replaces a whole character in a video from a single image. Genjutsu, the newest and most capable, has two modes: Motion Transfer rebuilds a new scene around a video’s motion, and Object Swap changes a selected character, outfit, product, location or object while keeping the rest of the shot.

Genjutsu takes “one input video up to 30 seconds long” with “up to 30 reference photos,” and outputs “up to 1080p.” A Lite version launched on 20 October 2026 for 4–30 second clips with up to 10 references. It’s available on the web and through Higgsfield’s API and MCP.

Pricing: Higgsfield publishes per-clip credit costs for Genjutsu. A 15-second Object Swap costs 48 credits ($2.35) at 480p, 112 credits ($5.49) at 720p and 320 credits ($15.68) at 1080p. Genjutsu Lite costs 96 credits ($4.70) at 720p and 192 ($9.41) at 1080p. Higgsfield’s plan prices change often and its pricing page did not load plan details for us, so check higgsfield.ai/pricing before you buy. Paid plans include commercial use.

Where it stops: video swaps are paid only, and 1080p swaps are expensive per clip. With three separate tools, it takes a minute to work out which one you need. For a fuller breakdown of the credit system, see Higgsfield pricing explained and Is Higgsfield AI free?.

VisionStory’s video face swap is the clearest about what it swaps. It has two modes: Face only (“replace the face while keeping the source body, outfit, and performance”) and Full body (“bring in the reference person’s face, hairstyle, and clothing while following the source performance”). Both keep the original scene and audio. Videos can run “up to 180 seconds (3 minutes)” at “up to 1080p,” and the face swap page says results carry no watermark.

Pricing: the Free plan gives 10 credits on sign-up plus a small weekly visit bonus. Pro is $9.99/month (120 credits), Advanced $29.90 (480 credits) and Ultra $99.90 (1,920 credits), with annual plans priced at 10 months. Paid plans include commercial use. VisionStory does not list the credit cost of one face swap on its pricing page.

Where it stops: a small free allowance, and no published cost per swap, so it’s hard to predict how many swaps a plan covers. It swaps people only, not objects or backgrounds.

Viggle is built for fun, shareable clips. It has “over 10,000 video templates” across sports, dance, K-pop, drama and memes, so you can pick a clip instead of finding one. You upload a face photo, and Viggle maps “your face, head shape, expressions, and full-body motion” onto the video. It handles “up to 5 characters in one upload” and runs on the web, iOS and Android.

Pricing: free accounts get daily free credits, with a watermark on the output. Pro is $7.99/month (shown discounted from $9.99) with 80 credits and videos up to 1 minute. Live is $15.99/month with 200 credits and videos
